text:
This analysis has moved



The analysis, code and results for the Mucor strains JEM1 and JEM2 are now kept in the MorenoLab repository. A public summary is at https://lab.stajich.org/MorenoLab_Mucor_Marchantia/. The full analysis is lab-only until the paper is published.

title: Candidate effectors of two Mucor strains isolated from Marchantia
text:
Summary
Two Mucor strains, JEM1 and JEM2, were isolated from the liverwort Marchantia. JEM1 is Mucor hiemalis and JEM2 is Mucor circinelloides (top ITS hit against UNITE v10, 99.3 % and 98.6 % identity). The study asks which of their secreted proteins could act as effectors and whether any could interact with host plant proteins. Every candidate is a computational prediction. None has been expressed or assayed.

title: DHN melanin and L-DOPA melanin genes in 23,376 BFD fungal genomes
text:
What this is, and where it stops being reliable




This is a working census of candidate genes, not a map of melanin production. Nothing here was tested at the bench. No call shows that a protein has the function of its step, and no absence call shows that a genome lacks the step. Both pathway files have verified: false, so every result is PROVISIONAL.
A target call means that a protein sits in a tree region bounded by the labelled leaves put in that step’s tree (references, decoys, named members, outgroups). The call depends on which leaves were chosen. It is not an ortholog call. For ayg1, mco_abr1, hmga, laccase_diphenol, tyrosinase and hppd the target holds almost every candidate, so the call carries little or no information beyond “the HMM hit”.
The tyrosinase and hppd trees have only 3 and 4 labelled leaves outside the target. “Tyrosinase placed” and “hppd placed” read as “family present”.
The PKS steps share one joint tree at identity 0.8. Its sampling is labelled not yet adequate (criterion C4 failed for 200 of 8,842 domains, section 4.2). Bootstrap support is from NNI-only searches, which are less optimised than standard searches. The effect on each support value is unverified. There is no outgroup in the PKS tree.
The tree for scytalone_dehydratase (v2) drops one leaf after the first tree was seen (selection with hindsight). The omt placement belongs to the mycosporine report and is not covered here.
The per-species comparison (section 6) uses placed-step calls only. Its presence rules are PROPOSED. A different reasonable rule moves the counts by thousands of species (section 6.3). The comparison reports counts only.
Gain and loss (section 7) cover the placed steps only. Co-loss of t4hn_reductase with four other DHN steps exceeds the matched null, with q floor 0.036 at N = 2,000. Model choice (ARD against ER) changes gain counts strongly.
Labels: MEASURED is read from a file named in the text. PROPOSED is a choice or a rule. UNVERIFIED is not checked.

title: DHN melanin and L-DOPA melanin genes in 23,376 BFD fungal genomes
text:
1. Findings so far
All numbers are MEASURED unless marked. Denominators: 23,376 searched genomes and 7,387 species with at least one searched genome (section 6.1).

The search covers every genome with proteins. 18 HMMs (15 are melanin steps) ran on 244,451,875 proteins in 23,376 genomes with no missing or duplicate genome. Of the 15 melanin steps, 12 are placed on a tree, 3 are PKS steps placed on one joint tree, and none is left as a search-hit step (section 3).
Step presence differs by clade. Placed tyrosinase calls are in 14,219 of 23,376 genomes (60.8 %), thn_synthase in 3,124 (13.4 %), heptaketide_pks in 2,091 (8.9 %), hexaketide_pks in 600 (2.6 %). Placed PKS calls are almost all in Ascomycota; placed tyrosinase calls are in Ascomycota (12,643 of 19,203) and Basidiomycota (1,491 of 3,242) (section 5).
The headline per-species comparison. Under the PROPOSED headline rules (D_pks, L_route), of 7,387 species: DHN only 133, L-DOPA only 2,933, both 1,725, neither 2,596. At genome level (23,376): 316, 9,232, 5,207, 8,621 (section 6).
The result depends on the rule. The strict yaml-route rule gives DHN only 2, L-DOPA only 3,969, both 689, neither 2,727 species. The wide rule (any placed step) gives 162, 1,714, 2,949, 2,562. The strict rule is small because no genome has all placed steps of the hexaketide or heptaketide route: 1,214 genomes have heptaketide_pks, ayg1, t4hn_reductase and scytalone_dehydratase placed and none of them has a placed t3hn_reductase (section 6.3).
The L-DOPA side is dominated by the tyrosinase family. L_route is positive in 14,439 genomes, of which 14,219 have placed tyrosinase. Without the tyrosinase family only 250 genomes are positive (laccase_diphenol 215 genomes, and 35 more genomes with both Asp-melanin steps; section 6.3).
The heptaketide PKS step has no target under the union decoy rule. Alb1, AlbA and wA cannot be separated in the tree (separated in 2 of 100 NNI bootstrap trees and 0 of 2 standard trees). The headline uses the per-step rule (the Alb1/AlbA/wA clade, target of 22 leaves, 2,123 of 2,200 candidate proteins in 2,091 genomes). The wA placement is unresolved (section 4.2).

2. The pathways, references and decoys






Sources



pathways/melanin_dhn.yaml (9 steps, 22 references, 40 decoy records) and pathways/melanin_ldopa.yaml (6 steps, 15 references, 33 decoy records); counts from docs/superpowers/notes/2026-11-23-melanin-mycosporine-step2.md, section 2 and section 9. Decoys of five steps were fetched from UniProt on 2026-11-23 (28 decoys; owner decision of the same day).


DHN melanin. The yaml has three PKS routes to 1,8-dihydroxynaphthalene and a polymerisation group. Route (a) pks_thn: thn_synthase, t4hn_reductase, scytalone_dehydratase, t3hn_reductase, scytalone_dehydratase. Route (b) pks_hexaketide: hexaketide_pks, ayg1, then the same four enzyme steps. Route (c) pks_heptaketide: heptaketide_pks, ayg1, then the same. The three PKS steps are alternatives, never consecutive. laccase_abr2 and mco_abr1 form the polymerisation group; the yaml says the order is not settled and the evidence is a colour phenotype only. The polymer is not a compound in the tables.
L-DOPA melanin. The yaml has four routes. tyrosinase_dopa: tyrosinase. laccase_exogenous: laccase_diphenol; its substrate comes from outside the fungus, so gene presence alone shows nothing about a pigment. pyomelanin: hppd. tyrosine_degradation: hppd, hmga; the yaml declares it “so that hmgA counts against pyomelanin”. asp_melanin: aspulvinone_e_synthase, asp_melanin_tyrosinase. Owner decision 6: hppd is reported as “family present”, not as a placed step. This report treats hmga the same way, because its placement carries no information (decision of 2026-11-24, “keep as is”).
Steps defined by reaction. The PKS steps are defined by reaction (thn_synthase, hexaketide_pks, heptaketide_pks; owner decision 9), plus an “any DHN PKS” column (D_pks, section 6). The owner did not answer whether to define them by pathway role instead; the yaml definition stays (open, section 8).

3. The genome-wide search (step 4)

18 HMMs (3 pathways), one combined cutoff table, 6 chunks of 4,000 genomes (the last has 3,376). The union of the searched lists is 23,376 genomes, 0 duplicates, 0 missing and 0 extra against has_proteins in genomes.tsv.zst. 244,451,875 proteins were searched (MEASURED, summary.txt).
Rows: DHN 62,329 rows in 53,024 proteins; L-DOPA 75,909 rows in 75,909 proteins. Genomes with at least one hit row: DHN 11,254, L-DOPA 19,073 (prefix counts; MEASURED).
The 5 re-annotated genomes. 39,700 proteins in 5 genomes have an id prefix that is not the locus tag of the genome table (F8B45790, FE750E90, FE41F6C9, FF465DA3, F6D07108; new prefixes F7CB232C, F317F9F5, FB9275E9, F629B7B9, FAD1592B). These genomes were re-annotated from new assembly versions and got new locus tags. The search covered all their proteins. Our copy maps the new prefixes to the old table rows with analysis/pathway_census/prefix_aliases.tsv; 13 of 13 unmapped hit rows map (11 to FE41F6C9, 1 to F8B45790, 1 to F6D07108). BUSCO and N50 in those rows describe the OLD assembly, and for FF465DA3 the new assembly has another accession. The BFD owner decides the real fix; this report does not change BFD files. Details: docs/superpowers/notes/2026-11-24-genome-prefix-mismatch.md.
Rows lost in placement (MEASURED, step 5 note, section 6): 11 melanin hit rows were not placed because the protein file for the new prefix is missing or the coordinates no longer match (ayg1 1, hppd 5, tyrosinase 5). The 5 genomes have no placed call for any step (Table 8, section 6.4).
A pathway is not “present” because of a hit. Many step HMMs are broad families: 84 % of genomes have a hit row for some step of the three pathways (19,645 of 23,376; including mycosporine steps).

Reading traps for Table 2:

A large target is not a result. tyrosinase: target 1,007 of 1,010 leaves (3 vertebrate outgroups outside); 50,447 of the 50,452 candidate rows are target (5 rows were not placed). hppd_v2: target 662 of 667 leaves. ayg1 11,835 of 11,835, mco_abr1 1,918 of 1,918, hmga 2,313 of 2,313 (one archaeal outgroup). In these steps the target says “near the references in a tree with few neighbours”.
The hppd split depends on the tree. With 300 representatives 5,850 candidates were target and 14,216 were on the decoy side. With all 662 clusters 14,212 of those 14,216 move into the target (MEASURED, step 5 note, 10.3). The v1 split was a property of the 300-representative tree.
tyrosinase v1 and v2 differ by 13 of 50,447 calls. The 1,000 representatives cover 48.3 % of the 50,447 domains by cluster. The all-placements run puts every one of the 14 earlier-unassigned queries into the target.
t3hn_reductase: the target has 5 leaves (3 references, 2 representatives), yet holds 2,236 of 2,240 candidates. Of its 250 representatives, 52 are nearest to a reference and 196 to a named member.
laccase_diphenol: the default epa-ng setting gave 204 of 402 unassigned. All placements give 402 target. The v2 row of other_steps_summary.tsv (198 target) is a record of the artefact. The all-placements row is used. The 402 proteins are 67 distinct sequences, and all lie in Cryptococcus (215 genomes).
aspulvinone_e_synthase and asp_melanin_tyrosinase. 83 of 168 and 42 of 2,471 candidates are target. The asp_melanin_tyrosinase floor is the score of the decoy ivoB, so most candidates (2,429) are on the decoy side; the 42 target proteins score 466.3 to 878.6. All target genomes of both steps are in Eurotiomycetes (49 and 42 genomes; step 5 note, section 3).
laccase_abr2 is rooted on one aligned decoy (P17489): 3,809 target, 5,822 decoy side.
scytalone_dehydratase v2: the first run (4 references, 8 named members) stopped, because the references did not form a clade free of a named member. The owner chose to drop that leaf (A0A2I2F2K6, cfoI) and rerun. The v2 target is bounded by 7 named members, with no decoy and no outgroup. This is selection with hindsight. It is UNVERIFIED whether another leaf choice would also separate the references.
hmga and hppd are family present. The only alignable non-target leaf for hmga is one archaeal protein of unknown function; the placement carries no information.



4.2 The three PKS steps on one joint tree

Tree and sampling. 559 leaves (identity 0.8: 532 cluster representatives, none drawn), 4,118 alignment columns, LG+G4, 2 raxml-ng starts, no outgroup (LovB, EryA1, yeast FAS1 and FAS2 failed the alignability rule). 9,374 candidate proteins: 994 hit one of the three PKS HMMs, 8,044 two, 336 all three (MEASURED).
Sampling label: not yet adequate. The criterion was written before the comparison (SAMPLING_CRITERION.txt). C1 (under 2 % of protein-step pairs change target status) passed with 0 of 15,890. C2 and C3 passed. C4 failed: 200 of 8,842 non-representative domains (2.3 %) lie outside identity 0.8 and coverage 0.8 of their representative (194 on identity, minimum 0.758; 6 on coverage). The criterion was not changed afterwards. Owner decision 10 accepted the label; no identity-0.9 rerun.
Bootstrap is NNI-only. One standard replicate takes 4.1 to 4.7 h; 100 would take about 70 to 80 h. The 100 replicates are NNI searches. On the same two resampled alignments the NNI tree differs from the standard tree by relative RF 0.113 and 0.129 and has a lower log-likelihood (by 727 and 522). NNI trees are less optimised than standard trees. The effect on each support value is unverified. Owner decision 2 accepted this for now.
Support (100 NNI replicates; FBP percent, TBE fraction). thn_synthase target node (240 leaves) FBP 88, TBE 0.997. hexaketide_pks target (56 leaves) FBP 99, TBE 0.999. The node that bounds the heptaketide target (22 leaves) FBP 100, TBE 1.000. The node that joins the four references of the three steps: FBP 66, TBE 0.965.
Heptaketide headline (owner decision 3). The heptaketide target is the Alb1/AlbA/wA clade under the per-step decoy rule: 22 leaves (Alb1, AlbA, wA and 19 representatives). It holds 2,123 of 2,200 candidate proteins in 2,091 genomes (Table 2). Beside it, the union rule (decoys of all three PKS steps pooled) gives no target. The union rule gives a target in 2 of 100 bootstrap trees, and the per-step rule in 100 of 100.
The wA placement is unresolved. Alb1 and AlbA are separated from wA in 2 of 100 NNI trees and in 0 of 2 standard trees. In the best tree the node of Alb1 and wA with 8 other leaves has FBP 50 and TBE 0.836, inside a 13-leaf node of all three (FBP 100). This supports “wA is unresolved as an outgroup of Alb1 and AlbA”. It does not show that wA makes YWA1 in any sense. wA stays in the target because the per-step rule does not use it as a boundary.
Per-step decoys do not change thn_synthase and hexaketide_pks. Their decoy sets equal the union (5 decoys), so the assign files are identical under both rules (cmp, MEASURED).
HMM hit and tree call differ. Of 6,316 proteins that hit both the thn_synthase and hexaketide_pks HMMs, 2,741 are in the thn_synthase target, 523 in the hexaketide_pks target and 3,052 in neither (0.7 run, hit_pattern_vs_target.tsv; the 0.8 run has the same pattern). No protein is target for two steps (0 of 9,374).
Dothideomycetes reading trap. 2,550 Dothideomycetes genomes have a thn_synthase hit row, and 5 have a placed call (0.7 run, PKS note section 6). Their proteins lie next to named leaves (nearest labelled leaf A7UMW1 for 13 of 24 representatives), which are outside every target by rule. So a missing PKS placed call in a class does not show that the class lacks a PKS.
Not covered by the epa-ng cap. The 2026-11-25 all-placements rerun changed 0 of 7,286, 8,604 and 2,200 PKS calls: the maximum number of placements per query was 6, so the PKS unassigned fractions (1.6 % to 3.2 % at identity 0.8) are not a cap artefact.



4.3 Overlaps between steps
MEASURED (tyrosinase_v2_laccase_target_overlap.tsv, sdr_target_overlap.tsv, the PKS target_overlap.tsv):

tyrosinase shares 0 proteins with the target sets of laccase_abr2, mco_abr1, laccase_diphenol and asp_melanin_tyrosinase. laccase_diphenol shares 0 proteins with laccase_abr2 or mco_abr1. laccase_abr2 and mco_abr1 share the same 4 proteins in 3 genomes.
At genome level (from the per-genome table of section 6): 0 genomes have both a placed tyrosinase and a placed laccase_diphenol; 0 genomes have a placed laccase_diphenol and a placed laccase_abr2; 3,205 genomes have a placed tyrosinase and a placed laccase_abr2 (different proteins).
For the comparison in section 6: laccase_abr2 and mco_abr1 are DHN steps (polymerisation group) and are not counted as L-DOPA evidence. The L-DOPA rules use only tyrosinase, laccase_diphenol, aspulvinone_e_synthase and asp_melanin_tyrosinase. So no protein is counted as evidence for both pathways through a shared target.
t4hn_reductase and t3hn_reductase: 583 proteins hit both HMMs; their target sets share 0 proteins (8,457 and 2,236); 974 of 11,667 candidate proteins are in neither.
No protein is a target for more than one PKS step (0 of 9,374).

10. What would change this, and what was not done
What would change the conclusions.

A known-ortholog test set for each step. If a step’s known members fall outside its target, the target boundary is wrong. If non-members fall inside, the call is too wide.
More labelled leaves for tyrosinase and hppd. A target that separates tyrosinase from other family members would change L_route from “family present” to a step call. Decisive test: add reviewed tyrosinase-family members of known other function (for example hemocyanin-like and catechol oxidase) as outgroups; if the target shrinks by thousands of proteins, the L-DOPA columns of Table 6 shrink with it.
A defined PKS outgroup (a separate investigation). Until then no statement about the order of divergence of the three PKS clades is supported.
A standard (non-NNI) bootstrap, or identity 0.9. If standard replicates separate Alb1 and AlbA from wA more often than 2 of 100, the heptaketide union-rule result would change.
A different step definition for the PKS steps (by pathway role). It would change which genomes count under D_route.

Not done here.

Gain and loss for the DHN versus L-DOPA species comparison (section 7 models each pathway separately; no cross-pathway event test).
PKS outgroup; resolution of wA; a hand check of the 157 + 118 unassigned PKS proteins.
Ortholog naming of any candidate. No literature check of any labelled leaf. No bench test.
The 45 other genomes whose protein file was rewritten with the same locus tag (the protein count differs between the carotenoid and melanin searches for 50 genomes: the 5 above and 45 more), and the 47 files newer than the genome table with an unchanged prefix, were not re-checked. Whether the 45 equal the 47 was not checked.
No BUSCO filter. The carotenoid pipeline measured that a BUSCO filter of 90 removes whole lineages (MEASURED 2026-11-22: Saccharomycetes 2,560 genomes to 0, Pichiomycetes 2,929 to 2; fig_presence_heatmap.py docstring). It is not applied here; not re-measured for these pathways.
No standard bootstrap for the PKS tree; no bootstrap for the 0.7 PKS tree. No second seed or tree for any non-PKS step. No tyrosinase tree above 1,000 representatives (the 1,000-representative tree covers 48.3 % of domains by cluster).
Mycosporine (separate report).
A test of the species collapse rule beyond any, all and single-genome species; no taxonomy re-curation of the BFD species names; no phylogenetic weighting.

Rendered reports from the DeltaGain analyses. Each page is generated from a REPORT.md that lives beside the code that produced it, in analysis/ — the page and the source therefore cannot drift.

title: DeltaGain: Reports
text:
Available

Delta Gain: findings synthesis
The novelty-yield measurement this project is named for: how much new protein-level information newly annotated fungal genomes add beyond UniProt and RefSeq. Whole-proteome funnel, what the surviving clusters are, family-level diversity against an order-matched null, and species accumulation across 23,567 genomes. Reproduced verbatim from the pipeline repository at a pinned commit.
One result on it has since been qualified — see the box at the top of the page, and its companion below.
Source: 1KFG/delta-gain @ 91eb5fe


The enriched-Pfam signal is mostly Y1000+ deposition
A companion test to the funnel’s largest family-level effect. 1,033 genomes from two UW-Madison Y1000+ BioProjects — 5.8 % of the new side — carry about three quarters of the enriched families’ novelty, because their proteins went to Figshare rather than to the protein databases the baseline is built from. Counting them as known inverts the effect. The random-Pfam controls barely move, which is what makes it a confound rather than a correction to everything.
Source: analysis/delta_gain_funnel/


Unspecific peroxygenases across 15,137 fungal genomes
A census of 97,520 PF01328 proteins, phylogenetic placement onto a 187-leaf reference tree, and a candidate list for expression. The report is as specific about what the model cannot do as about what it can: finding active-site residues is validated 95/95, ranking clade-V-like pockets works for ordering candidates, and predicting whether an arbitrary protein is an active peroxygenase is not reliable — out-of-clade AUC 0.556 on the 19 characterized enzymes the field has. It also reports four attempts to lift that ceiling that failed their own tests, and two errors found in the underlying genome database.
Source: analysis/enzymes_UPO/


Candidate effectors of two Mucor strains isolated from Marchantia
This analysis has moved to the MorenoLab repository. This page now carries a short public summary and a link to the new location. The full analysis is lab-only until the paper is published.


Fungal pigments: carotenoid, melanin and mycosporine pathways
A chapter on the four curated pigment knowledge bases: steps, evidence tiers per pathway, review errors that were caught, and the owner decisions that block a census. No gene census has been run; the chapter reports no gene counts. Under the strict evidence rule no carotenoid route and no complete DHN route is above tier T3. The fungal mycosporine references come from one species, Phaffia rhodozyma.
Source: analysis/pathway_census/PIGMENTS.md


Pathway knowledge base and the metabolite corpus
A record of what was tried when carotenoid, melanin and mycosporine pathways were curated as evidence-tiered tables and compared with the GNPS-processed metabolite corpus. The comparison was not run: the pre-set detectability gate failed for carotenoids, melanin, fucose and fungal MAAs (0 of 84 fungal-reference accessions show the main carotenoids). The page lists the failed design (mass shifts), the data errors that review caught, hypothesis status, and twelve rules for connecting the corpus to other data. Curation is unfinished and no step set has had owner review; corpus counts are reported by the EBC agent, not re-measured here.
Source: analysis/pathway_census/REPORT.md


Carotenoid biosynthesis genes in 23,376 BFD fungal genomes
The first census result for the carotenoid pathway: 14 step HMMs, the score check that sets each cutoff, a search of 244,451,335 proteins, and what a lower cutoff would add. It reports search hits, not genes. Tree placement was run for one step only, and the 5 reference proteins of that step lie inside a clade that holds 98.6 % of the candidates (10,708 of 10,863), so the placement cannot yet tell candidates apart. Every output is stamped PROVISIONAL. The page lists the negative results and what was not done.

title: Fungal pigments: carotenoid, melanin and mycosporine pathways
text:
1. Why these four pathways
The project began as two chapters for the fungal genome census, carotenoid and melanin biosynthesis, modelled on the earlier peroxygenase (UPO) chapter. Structure and affinity prediction was dropped. Mycosporines and mycosporine-like amino acids (MAAs) were added later because the metabolite corpus (held by the EBC agent) shows MAA library names in marine samples.
The working question was whether a genome that carries a pathway shows its product more often in the metabolite corpus. That comparison failed its pre-set detectability gate and was not run (section 5). The curated tables remain useful on their own as a reference for later census work.

title: Fungal pigments: carotenoid, melanin and mycosporine pathways
text:
2. How the tables are built
Each pathway has five flat tables in kb/<pathway>/: compound, reaction, reaction_participant, step, step_reaction. A step is a position in the pathway, defined by a protein family (Pfam, TIGRFAM or KO). A step_reaction row links a step to a reaction through one named protein of one named organism, with an evidence tier.







Tier
Meaning




T1a
The fungal enzyme was assayed, or its product was identified after heterologous expression. The quoted abstract sentence must name that protein and state an assay or product


T1b
Gene deletion or complementation with analysis of intermediates in the fungus


T1c
Deletion with a colour phenotype only


T2
Reaction shown for the same enzyme family in another organism


T3
Inferred from family or orthology, or a T1 claim whose quote fails the rule above


T4
Hypothesis with no direct evidence



A route tier that holds only across several organisms is not reported as a tier for any single organism.
An independent script (bin/verify_kb.py) re-fetches each accession, gene name, PubMed identifier, quoted sentence, sequence hash, ChEBI or PubChem identifier and formula, and checks them against the files. MEASURED result: 1,677 checks, 1,647 pass, 6 fail, 24 unchecked (kb/VERIFICATION_REPORT.md). A pass means the public record agrees with the file. It does not mean the biology is right.

title: The enriched-Pfam signal is mostly Y1000+ deposition
text:
What this is



A single targeted test, not a new analysis of the funnel. It asks one question of the funnel’s largest family-level effect — the enriched Pfam families’ +14.6-point excess over an order-matched null — and answers it by joining the existing cluster tables against NCBI BioProject metadata.
It is a companion to the funnel findings, which reports that effect in section 5.1. Read that page’s qualification box first if you have not.
The source of truth is analysis/delta_gain_funnel/ in this repository — code, tests, SLURM driver and the per-family output tables that the numbers below are computed from. This page renders REPORT.md from that directory, so the two cannot drift.
The report is explicit that it does not recompute the +14.6-point figure: doing that needs the order-matched null re-run with the Y1000+ genomes moved into the baseline, which has not been done. It shows the figure rests on a confound, which is a different claim.
2026-11-15. Code in analysis/delta_gain_funnel/bin/y1000_join.py, driver slurm/y1000_join.sh (job 32102558, 1 min 20 s), tests in test/ (17 passing). Per-family results in out/y1000_enriched.tsv and out/y1000_control.tsv.

title: The enriched-Pfam signal is mostly Y1000+ deposition
text:
The question
The delta-gain funnel’s largest family-level result is that Pfam families chosen for being enriched in new genomes carry +14.6 to +14.9 points more novel clusters than an order-matched baseline null, against +2.2 for size-matched random Pfam controls. The funnel’s own notes observe that the enriched list “is a Saccharomycotina yeast list” and read this as a lineage effect, supported by the fact that it replicates when the list is selected on one half of the species and evaluated on the other.
The objection the split-sample test does not answer: replication across species does not distinguish new biology from a shared deposition history. “Baseline” in the funnel means “had a prior NCBI annotation”. That is a boundary around a database, not around knowledge. A sequencing project that deposits assemblies to GenBank unannotated and releases its own proteomes elsewhere puts every one of its genomes on the new side, however long its proteins have been public — and it does so for all of its species at once, so a split-sample test replicates it perfectly.

title: The enriched-Pfam signal is mostly Y1000+ deposition
section: What this does and does not establish
text:
What this does and does not establish

It is not a recomputation of the +14.6-point figure. That statistic is a comparison against an order-matched baseline null with its own resampling; this is the raw novel-cluster share under two definitions of “known”. The direction and size are not in doubt, but the published number should be recomputed properly by re-running the order-matched null with Y1000+ in the baseline, not adjusted by hand from this table.
It covers 401 Pfam families, not the corpus. The funnel’s genome-wide figures (50.2 / 29.2 / 22.4 % novel at 95/70/50 %) are untouched by this run. Y1000+ is 5.8 % of the new-side genomes here, and its species are nearly all distinct, so some effect on the genome-wide numbers is likely — it has not been measured.
It does not show the enriched families are uninteresting. Yeast-specific families that Y1000+ sampled deeply are real biology; the claim it undercuts is that the funnel’s database comparison discovered them.
Y1000+ is the largest such project, not the only one. Any project depositing assemblies without annotation has the same effect. The same join against other large unannotated submissions would say whether this is one project or a general pattern, and that has not been run.

title: The enriched-Pfam signal is mostly Y1000+ deposition
text:
Consequence for the funnel
The funnel’s limitations already state that baseline is “a sampling, not a knowledge boundary” and that the enriched list “is selected on the outcome; it is a candidate list, not a genome-wide estimate.” Both are correct and both are now quantified: for this result the sampling boundary accounts for three quarters of it.
The honest summary of the enriched-Pfam result is that it measures where Saccharomycotina genomes were deposited, and that the lineage reading is not supported once deposition is controlled for. It should not be published as a novelty finding in its present form.

title: Unspecific peroxygenases across 15,137 fungal genomes
text:
What this is



A working analysis, not a finished study. Every clade call, site call and candidate here is a prediction from sequence and structure; no enzyme in this report has been expressed or assayed by us. Section 7 states the limitations and section 4 reports the results that came out negative, including four attempts to extend the model that failed their own tests.
The report is explicit about where it stops: identifying PF01328 sites is validated (95/95 against the published structure-based matrix), ranking clade-V-like pockets is reliable for ordering candidates, and predicting whether an arbitrary protein is an active peroxygenase is not reliable (out-of-clade AUC 0.556). Section 3 explains why that is arithmetic rather than something reanalysis can fix.
The source of truth is analysis/enzymes_UPO/ in the repository; this page renders REPORT.md from that directory, so the two cannot drift. The 45 documents it synthesizes are listed at the end, and the per-protein table it describes is in the repository beside the code that built it.
What exists, what can be called reliably, and what cannot.
2026-11-15. A synthesis of the UPO workstream. Every number here is produced by code in this directory and stated with its own evidence document; where a result is negative or bounded, the bound is given rather than the headline. The documents this draws on are listed at the end, and the per-document detail is the authority — this page is the route through them.
Unspecific peroxygenases (UPOs, Pfam PF01328) are secreted fungal heme-thiolate enzymes that transfer oxygen from H₂O₂ to unactivated C–H bonds. They do with a single cheap co-substrate what P450 monooxygenases need a reductase and NAD(P)H for, which is why they are of interest for synthesis. Fewer than thirty have been characterized biochemically.

title: Unspecific peroxygenases across 15,137 fungal genomes
text:
In short

The family is large and the catalytic machinery is common. 97,520 PF01328 proteins in 15,137 genomes; 34,561 (35.4 %) carry the full catalytic core.
Almost none of it is sequence-novel, and the apparent novelty is a deposition artefact. All 7,055 representatives have an nr hit. Apparent novelty is 2.0 % for RefSeq-annotated genomes and 18.7 % for GenBank-only ones (z = 7.4).
What is genuinely new is lineage coverage, not sequence. Whole well-supported clades of UPO-like proteins contain no characterized enzyme at all.
Active-site identification is reliable; activity prediction outside clade V is not. 95/95 agreement on site assignment against the published structure-based matrix; out-of-clade AUC 0.556 — chance — on predicting activity.
The clade caller refuses most of the database, by design. 78.9 % unassigned; 10.7 % carry a reliable call. Two independent callers agree 99.6 % above the trust boundary and 78.1 % below it.
Four attempts to break the ceiling all failed, and each failure was measured. Reference expansion made precision worse (80 % → 66 %); applicability distance failed as a confidence measure (p = 0.88); structural features from predicted models made the activity model worse (0.333); the Boltz-2 run hit its pre-declared kill switch and its 14 models were discarded.
Everything traces to one number: 19 characterized enzymes, three of five clades having one or two.
Two errors were found in BFD itself while building the candidate list — one of them affecting every consumer of the gene-model flags.

text:
2. Novelty is deposition, not biology
The workstream began as “are there new UPOs in early-diverging fungi?” The answer is largely no, and the way it is no is the interesting part.
Every one of the 7,055 catalytic-core representatives has a hit in nr. The apparent 18 % novelty splits cleanly by where the source genome was deposited: 2.0 % for genomes with a RefSeq (GCF_) annotation against 18.7 % for GenBank-only genomes, z = 7.4. A protein looks new when its genome’s proteins were never deposited in a form nr indexes.
This is the same effect, in a different family, as the one measured for the delta-gain funnel’s enriched-Pfam result, where counting the Y1000+ yeast genomes as public removes three quarters of the novelty (analysis/delta_gain_funnel/REPORT.md). Two independent analyses in this repository now put a number on the same confound.
Contamination was checked and is not the explanation: UPO genes sit on contigs more gene-rich than their genome’s typical contig (G1_FINDINGS.md §6).
What is new is lineage coverage. Several well-supported clades hold thousands of UPO-like proteins and not one characterized enzyme. That is what the candidate list targets.

The Boltz-2 run and its kill switch. The plan declared in advance that if predicted channel widths failed to reproduce the five experimental ones, the other 14 models would be discarded. They failed. The 14 models were discarded and the conclusion recorded is that this cannot be done with predicted structures at this scale.
The channel-width question, with its reversals recorded. CAVER 3.0.2 gave ~1 Å bottlenecks and the first conclusion was that the ring rule does not transfer. That was wrong — 3.0.2 has a documented bug placing the start vertex in too narrow a cavity. CAVER 3.0.3 reproduced the published ordering and gave r = +0.933 on four enzymes. Adding the fifth structure (TteUPO, 9IZ8 — the widest channel measured, zero activity) dropped it to r = +0.452. TteUPO can be set aside on grounds recorded before that measurement, but that is a post-hoc exclusion rescuing a correlation, and n = 4 is not evidence. CHANNEL_FINDINGS.md.
One positive worth keeping. Phase A found that Clade IV is the only clade whose promoter motifs replicate across independent lineages and survive both controls, including a CCAAT box naming the CCAAT-binding complex twice (HAP3, HAP5) — G3_FINDINGS.md. Phase B then found no co-regulation in RNA-seq. The motif result stands; the regulatory interpretation does not.

title: Unspecific peroxygenases across 15,137 fungal genomes
text:
5. What to assay
Three lists, answering different questions. They can be run together.
37 lineage candidates (CANDIDATES.md) — rules written and committed before the selection was run, in 8 pools across clade IV and six uncharacterized lineages, one protein per genus, one per 70 % identity cluster. A result in pool A or B is a first measurement for a lineage. Suggested first set: 12. Pool C (Glu180 absent — the lineage trait itself) waits on the structure question.
A 96-protein panel (ASSAY_PANEL.md) — 84 predicted active, 12 predicted inactive controls, 61 distinct pocket 5-mers, 79 species, 16 lineages, 93 % outside clade V. The controls are the point: GmaUPO-II shows the predicted-inactive cell is exactly where the model is known to fail, so assaying only predicted positives would measure precision and leave the false-negative rate unknown.
Six pre-registered external predictions (EXTERNAL_VALIDATION.md) — the cheapest experiment that would settle the model question. Six characterized UPOs already exist as purified enzymes elsewhere with no published 4-propylguaiacol number. Predictions recorded before any measurement: active DchUPO, DcaUPO; inactive CraUPO, MweUPO, PabUPO-II, UPO1_Codo. A failure among the predicted actives is the informative outcome — it would confirm the rule overcalls outside clade V, which is what the 0.556 warns about.
Decision D1 (Eurotiales sourcing for the Pichia construct) is recorded as moot: it rested on the pocket score, which does not predict anything of interest outside clade V (PLAN.md).

title: Unspecific peroxygenases across 15,137 fungal genomes
text:
6. Two errors found in BFD
Both were found while building the candidate list, and both are recorded for BFD rather than worked around here (bfd_findings/REPORT.md).
Start/stop-codon flags are wrong, database-wide. The shortlist’s gene-model rule removed Mucorales and Glomeromycota proteins wholesale (83 % and 75 % flagged incomplete). They are not incomplete. Splicing 5,816 models from the assemblies showed 99.3 % of flagged-missing starts and 99.8 % of flagged-missing stops are present; the true incomplete rate is ~0.2 %, not 10–60 %. The cause is case-sensitive codon matching against soft-masked genomes — a lower-case atg read as absent — which is why TAA stops are flagged missing more often (39.8 %) than TAG (18.8 %) or TGA (16.1 %). Fixed in Fungi_BFD fb1d7cd; gene_transcripts.parquet predates the fix. Any consumer that filtered on these flags silently dropped ~10 % of models BFD-wide and about half in Mucorales and Glomeromycota.
An ascomycete lineage inside a basidiomycete clade. 2,265 of the 6,378 members of Basidiomycetous 1st are Ascomycota, in 2,190 genomes — almost all single-copy, in 47.5 % of Dothideomycetes and all 67 Orbiliomycetes genomes, attaching as close to the references as the clade’s basidiomycete members and carrying the clade’s Asn180 at the same frequency (87.4 %). Zamocky noted one ascomycete transfer into this clade; this is two orders of magnitude more. Spread across thousands of independent genomes at single copy, it is not contamination, and it is not one recent transfer. It fits an old ascomycete UPO lineage. Placement cannot decide between nested (transfer) and sister (old lineage) because the reference holds only the basidiomycete diversity. The test that would settle it — an ML tree of ~150 + ~150 dereplicated members with two outgroups — is specified and not done.

title: Unspecific peroxygenases across 15,137 fungal genomes
text:
7. Limitations

Nineteen characterized enzymes. Three of five clades have one or two. 71 of 114 matched-identity test cases were impossible because removing a reference’s close relatives removed its whole clade.
One substrate, one assay, one publication. Task B’s calibration is 4-propylguaiacol conversion. It says nothing about which rings an enzyme cleaves — that is a separate measured negative.
Clade calls below ~55 % identity are not trustworthy under the old caller (precision 38 %), and BFD’s median identity to a reference is 43.8 %. The placement caller made no errors at matched identity down to <35 %, but on 19 enzymes.
69.6 % of BFD falls outside the calibration domain, and calib_domain is coverage, not confidence — it was tested as a confidence measure and failed.
No assay supports any rate or substrate range for any BFD protein here. catalytic_core means four residues are present: necessary, not sufficient.
Clade IV has one characterized member, so every clade IV row stays flagged +provisional_cladeIV; and clade IV’s status as a separate clade is unresolved (20–28 % bootstrap) even though the group is real (652/789 confirmed).
The shortlist should be re-run once the BFD tables are rebuilt; pools B4 and B5 were drawn from an eligible set shrunk by the flag bug. The 37 picks themselves stand.

title: Unspecific peroxygenases across 15,137 fungal genomes
text:
8. What would change this
More characterized enzymes. Every limit above traces to 19, and the alternatives were tested rather than assumed: expansion with inferred labels makes the caller worse, the structural route is calibrated on four, a second 4-PG panel does not exist, and labels from other papers are invalid because they are substrate-specific — PaDa-I, the field’s benchmark peroxygenase, converts 4-propylguaiacol at 1.7 %.
The six pre-registered assays are the cheapest move. The 96-well panel is the thorough one.

What this is, and where it stops being reliable




This is a working analysis of search hits, not a gene census. Steps 1 to 4 of the census plan are done (HMMs, score check, genome-wide search). Step 5 (tree placement, which decides what a hit is) was run for 11 of the 14 steps. It is a pilot for each of them. For phytoene_synthase, named lineage subclades cover only 22.8% of the candidates (section 6). For the five single-reference steps (cars, acaa, tsp3, tsp2, tdh), the target is a clade bounded by the labelled leaves put in the tree, not a set of orthologs (section 6f-2). No hit in this report is a called pathway gene.
Every output is stamped PROVISIONAL. The pathway definition has verified: false (refs/carotenoid/UNVERIFIED.md).
Nothing was tested at the bench. No BFD gene is shown to make a carotenoid.
A “candidate row” is one protein scored against one step HMM. One protein can give rows for more than one step. The number of distinct proteins was not counted.
Seven of the 14 step HMMs rest on one reference sequence. Their cutoffs are floors set by decoys, not by held-out references.
Owner decisions of 2026-11-23, all PROVISIONAL (the owner wrote “yes follow your recommendations”; the list is in docs/superpowers/notes/2026-11-22-owner-decisions.md, section 2026-11-23). (1) The one-reference target rule is accepted as provisional (section 6f-2). (2) crtr is shown as “family present” and is dropped from the step list. (3) carx stays as a search-hit step and is flagged as not placeable. (4) cars and tsp3 stay as two steps, and they are one protein set. (5) tdh uses the identity-0.8 run, with its caveat. (6) The floors of the single-reference steps are provisional and not validated.

1. Findings so far

The search covered every listed genome. 23,376 of 23,376 genomes were searched (244,451,335 proteins), with 0 genomes lost and 0 id-prefix errors. 987 of the 24,363 genomes in the table have no protein file and are excluded, not counted as absences (results/chunk_excluded.tsv).
No decoy and no reference of another step scores at or above a step’s own-reference minimum on any of the 14 step HMMs (0 rows in targets_at_or_above_min.PROVISIONAL.tsv). The test set is small: 69 decoys in total.
The search returned 238,898 candidate rows at the cutoffs used. The counts range from 12 rows (astaxanthin_synthase) to 46,698 rows (crtr). The large counts come from single-reference steps with low floors, so most of those rows are expected to be family members. This is a reading of the counts, not a measurement.
A higher cutoff for two steps hides a large number of low-scoring proteins. With a floor of 20 bits, astaxanthin_synthase returns 47,640 proteins and ylo1 20,276 proteins in 1,000 genomes. At the rule cutoff, the same run holds 2 and 458 proteins.
Step 5 pilot, phytoene_synthase and lycopene_cyclase: placement removes only a few candidates, and named lineage subclades cover a minority. In the second run, with 13 named fungal members and 7 non-fungal outgroups in the tree, 10,815 of 10,863 candidates (99.6%) fall in the target clade. Four named subclades exist (Dothideomycetes, Eurotiomycetes, Mucoromycetes, Ustilaginomycetes) and hold 2,482 candidates (22.8%). 8,333 candidates (76.7%) lie in the target clade but in no named subclade (section 6b). The cyclase step gives the same picture: 9,492 of 9,530 candidates in the target clade, 2,177 (22.8%) in a named subclade (section 6c). The result is “consistent with the HMM”, not “confirmed phytoene synthase”.
The candidates of phytoene_synthase are not squalene synthase. All 191 representatives score higher against the 5 synthase references than against a panel of 15 reviewed fungal squalene synthases (smallest margin 37.8 bits, median 128.1 bits).
The ggpp_synthase cutoff under-calls known GGPP synthases. 13 of the 39 reviewed fungal entries named geranylgeranyl pyrophosphate synthase score below it (26 of 39 found, 67%), including budding-yeast BTS1 (section 6e). The heatmaps now use placement of hits of 150 bits or more in the GGPP synthase clade instead (section 6f).
Single-reference steps: a new target rule gives a placement for five of them, and the assigned genomes are 92.8 to 96.6% Mucoromycetes. With one reference, the default target (smallest clade with the reference) is the reference leaf alone. The new rule takes the largest clade with the reference and no decoy, outgroup or named leaf (PROPOSED). It assigns 218 to 882 proteins per step in 263 to 292 genomes (section 6f-2). carx and crtr were not placed (section 6f-2).
A fifth step, ggpp_synthase, shares no gains or losses with the other steps beyond chance. It is present in 1,540 of 1,609 tips with data (96%), with 0 gains and 60 losses. Its co-loss with the three core steps (3 to 4 branches, all tip edges) has p 0.44 to 0.68 against a prevalence-matched null. The core result is unchanged: 62 to 69 shared losses against a null mean of 8 to 10 (section 6h).
Three of the 14 steps have no placement: carx, crtr and ylo1. The copy-number and phylum summaries (steps 6 to 8) wait for the placements to be reviewed.

text:
7. Negative and unresolved results

Single-reference steps cannot be checked for sensitivity. Seven steps (acaa, cars, carx, crtr, tdh, tsp2, tsp3) have one reference. Removing it leaves nothing to score, so there is no held-out value. More references would help; a structure model would not.
The held-out check is weak for near-identical references. For astaxanthin_synthase the lowest held-out score is 1332.5 and the lowest own score is 1343.2, because the two references are almost the same sequence. The cutoff therefore says little about distant homologs. The 25% reduction is a test of this, not a fix.
The lycopene cyclase decoys test the cutoff weakly. The highest decoy score is 29.3 and the lowest held-out reference score is 174.1. Any cutoff in between is consistent with the decoys, and none was tested on a genome (refs/carotenoid/decoys/LYCOPENE_CYCLASE_DECOYS.md).
A same-function homolog from Archaea (Q9HNE5) scores 115.6 on the cyclase HMM. It is a tree outgroup only, not a decoy, so it does not set the cutoff (refs/carotenoid/outgroups/).
The first step 5 design did not discriminate for phytoene_synthase, and adding named members helped only partly. In the first run the clade of the 5 references was too broad and every support was high, so placement removed only the 155 candidates on the decoy side. With 13 named members and 7 outgroups, four classes form named subclades, but 76.7% of candidates (8,333 of 10,863) stay in the target clade with no named subclade, and Sordariomycetes, the class of two references, forms none. The expectation that the candidates would include many squalene synthases was wrong: all 191 representatives score higher against the references than against 15 reviewed fungal squalene synthases (bin/check_paralog_panel.sh, paralog_panel/summary.tsv: smallest margin 37.8 bits). The 4 decoys probe the root of the tree, not the candidate set.
The first two lycopene_cyclase trees stopped by their own check (2026-11-22). The tool refuses to go on when the 5 references do not form a clade free of decoys and outgroups. This was a design error of ours, not a biological result. In the first tree, 5 decoys (the four PF05834 proteins and Q9KK79) lay inside the clade of the references; they have no detectable homology to the fungal cyclase domain (refs/carotenoid/decoys/LYCOPENE_CYCLASE_DECOYS.md), so they cannot be aligned. A filter that kept decoys scoring at least 10 bits left Q9KK78, which aligns over only 44 of 241 HMM positions (18%) and also fell inside the fungal clade (pendant branch 3.8). The rule now also needs a coverage of at least 50% of the HMM, which keeps no decoy. The decoys still serve the cutoff and the absence check. The first two folders are kept as records (lycopene_cyclase/, lycopene_cyclase_v2/attempt2_decoy_Q9KK78/).
A measurement in the decoy notes does not reproduce. The decoy notes list step-HMM scores of 10.1 for A1XI29 and 12.9 for Q93QX4. A new hmmsearch of the cyclase HMM against the 9 decoys (E-value limit 1000 for sequences and domains, HMMER 3.4) reports only Q9KK78 (29.3 bits). The cause was not found. The tree filter uses the value that reproduces.
The default target rule gave no target for a single-reference step (2026-11-23). In the first cars run the target was the reference leaf, and 0 of 1,804 candidates were called target. This is a property of the rule, not a biological result. The new rule fixes it (section 6f-2), and its target depends on which labelled leaves are in the tree.
tdh at the default clustering identity gave a 6-leaf tree. The 6,142 domains fell into 2 clusters at identity 0.5. The run at 0.8 gave 262 clusters. The first run is kept as a diagnostic result (section 6f-2).
carx cannot be placed and crtr cannot be separated from housekeeping reductases. No alignable non-target leaf exists for carx (best 35.3 bits, coverage at most 0.19). For crtr, 98.5% of genomes have a hit and the HMM scores 10 reviewed fungal NADPH-cytochrome P450 reductases at 448.4 to 1009.6 bits (section 6f-2).
The metabolomics corpus cannot test carotenoids. REPORTED by the EBC side: 0 of 84 fungal-reference accessions show beta-carotene, zeaxanthin or canthaxanthin (docs/superpowers/notes/2026-11-21-exploration-log.md, section 1). This is a statement about the corpus, not about BFD genomes.

section: 8. What would change this, and what was not done
text:
8. What would change this, and what was not done
What would change the findings. More named members from lineages that have none yet (Sordariomycetes outside the 5 labelled leaves, Agaricomycetes, early-diverging groups) would show whether the 8,333 unnamed candidates split into groups. Named members with experimental evidence would let a subclade name stand for function. A rerun with more raxml-ng starts and with the outgroups rooted without the squalene synthase decoys would test the root. A decoy or a non-pathway family member that places inside a target clade would show that a step’s HMM cannot separate it. A reference set with more members for a single-reference step would change its floor.
Not done here:

Step 5 for carx, crtr and ylo1 (sections 6f-2 and 2). The other 11 steps have a placement (sections 6, 6c, 6c-2, 6f, 6f-2). The lycopene_cyclase tree has no decoy, and the five single-reference trees have targets bounded by few labelled leaves.
The single-reference steps are in the heatmaps (figures 7 and 8) as placed columns. cars and tsp3 are still two columns, labelled “same set”, and are not merged. carx and crtr are not placed in the figures. The figures show assigned calls only; they do not show copy number.
Quality, contamination and haplotype flags (step 7). There is no fungal versus non-fungal reference set, so counts will be raw first.
The copy matrix and phylum summary (step 8), the deposited versus BFD comparison (steps 9, 10), the tblastn absence check (step 11) and triage (step 12).
Co-gain and co-loss, beyond sections 6g and 6h. Not done: the single-reference steps were not added to the gain/loss analysis; a test of whether the whole-lineage ggpp_synthase absences (Schizosaccharomycetes, Wallemiomycetes) are a cutoff or divergence effect; a yeast-specific BUSCO set (the 65 to 70 floor cannot catch an incomplete yeast assembly); the simulation null on a second tree or at cutoff 65; replicate genomes per genus; and the same analysis for the other steps. No completeness filter is applied in the main results (owner decision, 2026-11-23); the BUSCO 65 and 70 runs are a sensitivity check.
The root of the genus tree is the owner’s choice (Blastocladiomycota, with Microsporidia dropped); a second root on Chytridiomycota gives identical counts. The simulation null was not run for run C (all tips, Blastocladiomycota root), and Pagel was not re-run for the cart pairs on the new tree.
The question of whether fungal lycopene cyclases have diversified in some groups (docs/superpowers/notes/2026-11-22-open-questions.md, Q1). It needs step 5 first.

title: Mycosporine biosynthesis genes in 23,376 BFD fungal genomes
text:
What this is, and where it stops being reliable




This is a working analysis of search hits and tree placements, not a gene census and not a map of mycosporine producers. Steps 1 to 5 of the census plan are done for three steps: ddgs, omt and atp_grasp_ligase. The other two steps of the pathway file, mg_glucosyltransferase and glutamicol_formation, have no known gene and no reference. They were not searched (section 2). So no genome in this report can be called a producer of any mycosporine. The main fungal compound, mycosporine-glutaminol-glucoside, needs the glucosylation step, and that step cannot be searched.
Every output is stamped PROVISIONAL. The pathway file has verified: false. No step has a verified fungal reference: 6 of the 8 references are not verified, and the verified two are cyanobacterial (refs/mycosporine/UNVERIFIED.md).
Nothing was tested at the bench. The only fungal genes with an assay are the three genes of one cluster in Phaffia rhodozyma UCD 67-385 (PMID 36983003, abstract and full text read by the curator).
Only one step has a tree placement that separates anything: omt, and only as a single-reference placement. The step has 2 references. The placement used the Phaffia OMT alone as the target and put the Nostoc MysB in the tree as a named leaf. The target is a region of a tree, bounded by 3 decoys and 6 outgroups. It is not a set of tested mycosporine O-methyltransferases (owner decision 5 of 2026-11-25).
ddgs is placed, but 8,864 of 8,865 candidates fall in the target. The placement shows that the candidates lie near the references. It does not separate DDGS from other members of the family.
atp_grasp_ligase is not placed. No alignable non-target sequence exists (section 5d). Its call is a search hit.
Counts are genomes with at least one protein that passes the cutoff or the placement. A genome with no call may have an incomplete assembly or a diverged gene. Absence is not shown.
Labels: MEASURED is read from a file named in the text. PROPOSED is a choice or an estimate. UNVERIFIED is not checked.
Owner decisions are listed in section 9. All of them keep the PROVISIONAL stamp. Decisions of 2026-11-23, 2026-11-24 and 2026-11-25 apply. Two items are still open (section 9).

text:
1. Findings so far

The search covered every listed genome. 23,376 of 23,376 genomes with a protein file were searched (244,451,875 proteins), with 0 duplicates, 0 missing and 0 extra genomes. 987 of the 24,363 rows of the genome table have no protein file and are excluded, not counted as absences (MEASURED, results/search/melanin_myco_full/summary.txt; the 24,363 is from docs/superpowers/notes/2026-11-24-genome-prefix-mismatch.md, section 4).
One check failed and was repaired in our copy only. 39,700 proteins in 5 genomes carry a locus tag that is not the one in the genome table, because BFD re-annotated those genomes. All 39,700 were searched. An alias file maps 13 of 13 affected candidate rows back to their genome row (section 3).
The search returned 32,474 candidate rows for the three steps, on 32,422 distinct proteins, in 12,739 of 23,376 genomes (54.5%): omt 14,441 rows, atp_grasp_ligase 9,167 rows and ddgs 8,866 rows. The counts match the 200-genome projection within a ratio of 0.91 to 0.99 (MEASURED, section 4). A row is one protein scored against one step HMM.
Cutoffs are weak for two of the three steps. The omt cutoff is an owner override (100.6), not a value derived from references. The rule value is 8.3, and it is below all five decoys. The atp_grasp_ligase cutoff (105.0) is set by a cyanobacterial reference held out of its own HMM, and no decoy scores on that HMM. Only ddgs has a margin that a decoy test supports: lowest held-out reference 463.5 against highest decoy 315.5 (section 2).
ddgs is placed in 8,760 genomes (37.5% of 23,376) and omt in 10,446 (44.7%). The atp_grasp_ligase hit is in 8,859 (37.9%). All three calls are present in 7,793 genomes (33.3%): 7,657 of 19,203 Ascomycota (39.9%) and 136 of 3,242 Basidiomycota (4.2%). No other phylum has a genome with all three. These are calls of protein families that are widely distributed. They are not mycosporine-pathway calls (section 7).
The omt placement does not follow the score. Of 14,439 placed candidates, 11,730 are target and 2,703 are on the decoy side. The median score is 112.5 for the target and 108.6 for the other side. 10,097 of the 14,441 rows lie between 100.6 and 120.7, the band where the floor was moved (section 5c).
Genera named in the literature give a mixed picture. In 12 Phaffia genomes, 7 have all three calls and 5 have none. In 16 Cystobasidium genomes, ddgs is placed in 16 and omt is a search hit in 16, but the omt target call is present in 0 (section 7).
Gain and loss (section 8) covers ddgs and omt only. Co-loss is 79 branches against a matched null mean of 16.68 (q 0.002), but 73 of the 79 are tip edges and internal-edge co-loss is within the null interval. The null does not model missing data.

The ddgs and omt columns are not independent measures of a pathway. The families are broad. Genome count follows sequencing effort: Sordariomycetes (5,981 genomes), Eurotiomycetes (3,201) and Pichiomycetes (2,929) are large because many strains were sequenced. Limits of this section




Only ddgs and omt are modelled. ddgs is placed, but 8,864 of 8,865 candidates are in the target, so its call is close to a search hit. The omt target is one tree region from one reference, not a tested enzyme. atp_grasp_ligase is a search-hit step and is not modelled.

10. Negative and unresolved results

The first omt placement stopped. The references do not form a clade free of decoys and outgroups, because the Phaffia OMT and MysB are 17% identical (job 32435495, return code 3). This was a property of the reference set, not a failed run. The single-reference placement replaces it and changes what the target means (section 5c).
The omt floor is a decoy floor, not a derived cutoff. The rule value (8.3) is below all five decoys. 48 of 50 sampled reviewed fungal O-methyltransferases have no hit at E-value 1000 or lower on the omt HMM. Of 801 reviewed fungal entries with EC 2.1.1, 5 hit and 1 (Q8NKC1) scores at or above 100.6. No true mycosporine OMT other than the Phaffia protein is known, so this does not measure how many real orthologs the floor loses (UNVERIFIED; step 2 note, section 9.5).
The omt tree call is not a score split. Medians differ by 3.9 bits (112.5 and 108.6), and 75.5% of the low-band candidates are in the target. The tree has 3 decoys, 6 outgroups and 1 named leaf. A larger set of labelled O-methyltransferases could move candidates between sides. This was not tested.
atp_grasp_ligase cannot be placed. 0 of 6 decoys and 0 of 1,111 reviewed ATP-grasp entries align (section 5d).
ddgs placement separates almost nothing. 8,864 of 8,865 are target. This happens when the labelled leaves are few. It is not a pass of a specificity test.
The atp_grasp_ligase and ddgs cutoffs rest on one fungal reference each. For ddgs the lowest held-out score is the Phaffia reference (463.5). For atp_grasp_ligase it is a cyanobacterial reference (105.0). The two Phaffia ATPG sequences are 98% identical, so they are not independent.
A search without a cutoff shows no near-miss in Rhodotorula (MEASURED, 2026-11-26). All 215 Rhodotorula genomes with protein files have a best ddgs domain score of 68.5 to 109.8 bits (median 102.2). The cutoff is 463.5, so the best score is 353.7 bits below it. The best hits cover 0.57 to 0.64 of the HMM, and genomes with a ddgs call cover about 0.98. Lowering the cutoff by 10%, 25% or 50% adds 0 Rhodotorula genomes. 5 of 12 Phaffia genomes show the same pattern (94.3 bits, coverage 0.58), as do Cystofilobasidium (8 of 8), Rhodosporidiobolus (14 of 14) and Sporobolomyces (22 of 22). This does not show that these genomes lack a ddgs gene: only predicted proteins were searched, and the best 100-bit hit was not identified. Details: docs/superpowers/notes/2026-11-26-rhodotorula-ddgs-check.md.
The literature check of genera gives a mixed result. Cystobasidium has no omt target call, and Rhodotorula has no ddgs call (section 7). Both could mean a cutoff or target that is too narrow for non-Phaffia lineages, or different enzymes. No test separates the two readings.
No bench or metabolomics support. The mycosporine genes of non-Phaffia fungi are not assayed. No metabolomics data were used for mycosporines here.
The PKS tree support caveat does not apply (no PKS step in this pathway). Placement trees here are single-seed trees with no bootstrap.

One result on this page has since been qualified



Section 5.1 reports that enriched Pfam families show new genomes adding far more novelty than an order-matched baseline null — +14.6 to +14.9 points at 70 % identity, against roughly +0.4 to +2.2 for CAZy, MEROPS and random-Pfam controls. It is the largest effect in the document.
A later test shows that most of that excess is where the genomes were deposited, not what is in them. Two UW-Madison Y1000+ BioProjects contribute 1,033 genomes — 5.8 % of the new side — and they carry about three quarters of the enriched-family novelty. Their assemblies went to GenBank in 2024 but their proteins went to Figshare, so the proteins are public and yet absent from the nr baseline this analysis screens against. Counting them as known turns the enriched families’ +24.8-point excess over the controls into a 23.1-point deficit.
Read the test → The enriched-Pfam signal is mostly Y1000+ deposition
What that test does not do is re-run the order-matched null with those genomes moved into the baseline, so the +14.6 figure below has not been recomputed — it has been shown to rest on a confound. The other family sets are far less affected: the median family loses 86.6 % of its novelty among the enriched families and 0.8 % among the random controls. Sections 3 and 4, which are whole-proteome rather than family-level, are not touched by this.

title: Delta Gain: findings synthesis
section: 1. The question and the short answer
text:
1. The question and the short answer

How much NEW protein-level information do newly annotated fungal genomes add, compared with what was already known from previously annotated fungal genomes, controlling for the many re-sequenced strains of the same species?

Baseline = 5,703 genomes with a prior NCBI annotation. New = 17,864 matched genomes without one (183.1 M proteins). About 60 % of new genomes are strains of species already in the baseline.
Short answer.

Whole-proteome view. 50.2 / 29.2 / 22.4 % of new proteins fall in clusters with no baseline member at 95 / 70 / 50 % identity. That protein-weighted headline understates novelty per species and is dominated by heavily resequenced species. Counted once per species about 39 % of proteins are novel at 50 % identity, and the novelty comes from new species and genera, not from new strains.
Strains add little. Strains of baseline species are 60 % of new proteins but 36 % of the novel ones (13.3 % novel at 50 %, median genome 5 %). New species in a baseline genus are 27.6 % novel; new genus or higher 57-63 %.
Most novel proteins are still homologs of known families. Of the survivor clusters seen in 5 or more genomes, 79 % have a detectable baseline homolog by sensitive search; 10.7 % have none. Among all 12.2 M single-genome clusters 63 % have a homolog and 21 % none.
Novel protein mass is species-restricted. 82 % of survivor clusters (61 % of survivor proteins) come from one species.
Within a family, new genomes add about what the same number of baseline genomes would. For typical CAZy, MEROPS, random Pfam and secondary-metabolism backbone families the extra is about 1-3 percentage points. Pfam families chosen for being enriched in new genomes (mostly Saccharomycotina yeast families) show about +15 points, and that replicates in independent species.
Unseen clades are not special. New genomes from orders with no baseline genome are no more novel than a typical held-out baseline order (pooled and class-matched nulls, about -2 points at 70 %).
Artefacts do not explain the result. Predictor mismatch (NCBI vs BFD gene models) adds 1.5-3 points; contamination-flagged genomes supply 8.2 % of novel protein mass; annotated transposons about 1 %; there is no excess of prokaryote-like best hits among novel proteins.
Novel family members are often degenerate or partial. Novel GH18 and S08 regions are shorter and more often miss catalytic residues; novel S08 hits include probable carboxylase false hits. These are not evidence of new catalytic function.
The fungal 50 % cluster pangenome is not saturated. Adding species in random order, each further species still contributes about 2.7-4.5 thousand new clusters. A new species adds about five times more clusters per genome than a resequenced strain of a known species (about 1,870 vs 350).
No secretome or expansion signal. New genomes do not carry more signal peptides or small-secreted-protein candidates than same-order baseline genomes, survivors are not enriched for them, and CAZy/MEROPS copy number changes are small and balanced (19 families expand, 23 contract per 1,000 proteins).
The family result is robust. It does not change with coverage threshold, coverage mode or Pfam region definition (five families, sensitivity run).

3.3b Species accumulation of 50 % clusters (E4)
All 23,567 genomes with annotated proteins (237 M distinct genome x tier-50 cluster pairs, 33.4 M clusters) were grouped into species units: 2,778 baseline species, 822 new-genome groups of species that also have a baseline genome (N_known, about 10.7 k mostly resequenced genomes) and 4,632 new species (N_newsp, about 7.2 k genomes). Units were added in random order (20 permutations per ordering) and each cluster was credited to the first unit that contains it (bin/accumulation.py, results/accumulation/; figure figures/E4_accumulation.svg).



Species accumulation



No saturation. The curve is close to linear. After all 2,778 baseline species (16.25 M clusters) each further species still adds about 4.0-4.5 k clusters at the start of the new units (positions 2,776-3,200), declining only to about 2.7 k for the last 230 new species. The 50 % cluster pangenome of the fungal kingdom is open at this sampling depth.
Baseline-first ordering. New units add 17.14 M clusters absent from the baseline (matches the 17.10 M survivor clusters counted independently; the small gap is clusters held only by genomes outside the two classes): 3.72 M from the 822 resequenced-species groups (about 350 clusters per genome) and 13.42 M from the 4,632 new species (about 1,870 clusters per genome). Strains of known species add little per genome; new species add roughly five times more.
New-first ordering (contrast). The first 2,778 random new species cover 13.5 M clusters, 17 % fewer than the 2,778 baseline species (16.2 M). The 5,454 new species together cover 22.2 M clusters, and the baseline still adds 11.2 M clusters after all new genomes (about 4.0 k per baseline species). The baseline therefore carries a large share of sequence space that the new genomes do not reproduce.
Caveat. Baseline proteins are NCBI gene models and new proteins are BFD models, so cluster counts per species include the 1.5-3 point predictor effect and differences in proteome size and completeness; the curves describe species sampling of 50 % clusters, not new families (most clusters are small and lineage-restricted, see section 4).

Predictor mismatch. 300 baseline genomes scored as NCBI vs BFD annotations against the same 1,000-genome reference: novel fraction 57.3 -> 60.0 / 34.5 -> 35.8 / 25.7 -> 26.8 % (95 / 70 / 50 %). The gene-model difference inflates novelty by about 1.5-3 points.
Contamination and transposons. Genomes with GC more than 8 points from their order median (1,067) or BUSCO < 50 (322) are 6-7 % of new genomes and give 8.2 % of novel protein mass. Annotated TE domains label about 1 % of survivor proteins.
Horizontal transfer / contamination screen. Best Swiss-Prot hit of survivor representatives (metagenome-bin genomes excluded) is prokaryotic for 4.1-4.8 % of survivors vs 5.2 % of background proteins; at >= 40 % identity 1.0-1.3 % vs 1.3 %. No enrichment. This is a screen only (< 50 % of survivors have a Swiss-Prot hit; no phylogeny).

ESMFold (single sequence) on 400 representatives of no-hit profile clusters vs 400 of profile clusters that did gain a baseline hit: mean pLDDT (0-1) 0.372 vs 0.440; share with pLDDT >= 0.5: 8.8 % vs 27.3 %; >= 0.7: 0.8 % vs 6.3 %. Novel no-hit proteins are predicted with lower confidence, but both sets are low and length differs (150 vs 190 aa), so this fits disorder, orphan or spurious-model status without proving it. Not run at full scale.


4.4 Secretome and lineage-specific expansions (E7)
Species-level units (genomes of one species and class averaged), contrast within order (71 orders with at least 3 units of each class), permutation test inside orders. Details and thresholds: docs/E7_RESULTS.md.

Secretome. Whole-proteome signal-peptide fraction is 7.64 % in new vs 7.71 % in baseline genomes; small-secreted-protein (SSP) candidates (signal peptide, <= 300 aa, >= 4 Cys, no GPI anchor, no transmembrane helix beyond a signal anchor) are 1.369 % vs 1.359 %. Within order, new genomes carry slightly fewer signal peptides (-0.14 points, p 0.0003) and SSP candidates (-0.04 points, p 0.0003); the effect comes from new species (-0.045 points), not from new strains of known species (+0.001, p 0.94). The SSP rule is a heuristic, not an effector call.
Survivors are not enriched for secreted proteins. Observed / expected SSP among survivor representatives (expected from the same genome’s rate): 0.88 (1 genome), 0.98 (2-4), 1.01 (5-19), 0.79 (20 or more); signal-peptide obs/exp 0.72-0.90.
Copy number. For 323 CAZy and MEROPS families seen in at least 50 genomes, per 1,000 proteins, 19 families expand and 23 contract in new genomes (q < 0.05), with small effects (4-15 % relative for common families). On raw copies per genome 174 families appear contracted, but new proteomes are about 8 % smaller (10.2 k vs 11.1 k proteins), so the proteome-size-normalised comparison is the fair one. Lineage-specific expansion is not a general property of the new genomes. Counts are proteins with a hit, not independent duplications.

5.1 Do new genomes add more than the same number of baseline genomes?
F3 (order-matched baseline-vs-baseline null): across the pilot families, the wide run (340 CAZy, 174 MEROPS, 200 enriched Pfam; 717 families, 18.0 M regions) and the subfamily run (474 subfamilies), new genomes add about the same novelty as equally many same-order baseline genomes.

The family ranking (S08 > GH18 > AA9 > controls) is already present in the null: it reflects inherent family diversity, not the new genomes.
The enrichment effect replicates in independent species: lists selected on half of the species and evaluated on the other half give +14.6 points vs +4.3 for random controls, so it is not a winner’s-curse artefact. The enriched list is a Saccharomycotina yeast list; BUSCO of those orders is 75-80 %, so this is a lineage effect rather than a quality flag.



5.1b Sensitivity to clustering and region choices (E9)
Five families (GH18, S08, the ketosynthase PF00109, one enriched Pfam PF10450, one random-control Pfam PF01568) were re-clustered and re-nulled (1,010 genomes per side, 200 draws) with later-tier coverage 60 / 80 / 90 %, target-only instead of bidirectional coverage, and Pfam regions by alignment span instead of envelope (Pfam families only; CAZy and MEROPS have one span definition). The 30 % tier is already a default tier. Details: docs/E9_RESULTS.md.

The family-level result is insensitive to these choices. New minus null at 70 %: GH18 +0.010, S08 +0.004, PF00109 0.000, control +0.001, with variants differing from the default by at most 0.004-0.007, far inside the null intervals.
The enriched family keeps its excess in every variant: PF10450 +0.095 to +0.101 at 70 % (intervals exclude 0 in all five variants) and +0.065 to +0.074 at 50 %, so the enrichment is not an artefact of one clustering setting.
The 30 % tier adds no signal: all differences within +-0.02 with intervals spanning 0. Across 15 family x tier cells there is one sign flip, PF10450 at 30 % with alignment-span regions (-0.007 vs +0.018), with every interval spanning 0.
Limits: five families, small families (4-6 k regions) have wide intervals, and only clustering and region definition were varied (not the search sensitivity, the first-tier coverage, the null design or upstream annotation thresholds).



5.2 Unseen clades
Leave-one-order-out (F3b): holding out a whole order is far more novel than the within-order null (c70 median 60-85 % for the diverse families), but new genomes from orders with no baseline genome are not more novel than a typical held-out baseline order (CAZy/MEROPS c70 -6.8 / -6.4 points pooled; class-matched F3c -1.9 / -1.9 / -1.0 points for CAZy / MEROPS / Pfam). The family-level novelty of new taxa is what sampling any unseen clade gives, not a special property of these genomes. Caveat: only four classes allow the class-matched test, with 5 genomes per draw.


5.3 Where the novelty sits
Novelty is clade-specific, not family-wide: GH18 is 7.0 % novel overall but 2.9 % in Hypocreales and 2.1 % in Eurotiales vs 72.8 % in Ascoideales, 34.4 % in Pichiales and 23.0 % in Boletales; S08 is 5.0 % in Hypocreales vs 31.1 % in Agaricales. text:
6. Lifestyle correlates
FungalTraits 1.2 genus labels (Põlme et al. 2020) cover 1,061 of 1,204 genera with a new genome (16,085 of 17,865 genomes). Unit = genus; within-order deviation in novel fraction at 50 %, permutation test inside orders. All genomes: mycorrhizal +4.4 points, saprotroph +1.2, plant pathogen -3.9, animal-associated -2.8 (n.s.), yeast growth form -4.1. Holding relatedness fixed, only mycorrhizal remains (+7.5 points among new species in a baseline genus; +2.0 among new genera or higher); plant pathogens stay at -3.0 among distant genomes. Most lifestyle differences are sampling depth and relatedness, and lifestyle is nested in clade, so this is a screen, not a causal result.

title: Delta Gain: findings synthesis
text:
7. Limitations

Baseline definition. “Baseline” is “had a prior NCBI annotation”. It is a sampling, not a knowledge, boundary: the baseline is enriched for model organisms and well-sampled clades.
Strain pseudo-replication. Handled by rarefaction, species-collapsed variants and genus-level units, but any protein-weighted number is dominated by heavily resequenced species.
Predictor. The funnel mixes NCBI baseline proteins with BFD new proteins (1.5-3 points); the family walk uses BFD annotation for both groups and avoids this.
Selection. The enriched Pfam list is selected on the outcome; it is a candidate list, not a genome-wide estimate.
Family nulls only cover orders present in both groups; the clade-matched F3c has few classes.
Labels and searches use cluster representatives; sensitive-search hits indicate homology, not function. No-hit clusters are a mix of orphan genes and gene-model artefacts that this work cannot separate.
Proxies. The HGT screen (Swiss-Prot taxonomy) and the BGC-backbone analysis (domain level) are cheaper stand-ins for a phylogeny-based HGT analysis and for antiSMASH.

1. The question and why it changed
The first request was two analysis chapters for the fungal genome census: carotenoid biosynthesis and melanin biosynthesis (DHN and L-DOPA), modelled on the earlier peroxygenase (UPO) project. Structure and affinity prediction was dropped. Gene copies were kept as a ranking for later functional testing.
The request then grew. The owner asked for a public-knowledge knowledge base, as flat tables, of what fungal enzymes can make (upstream and downstream), and a comparison with the processed metabolite corpus. Mycosporines and mycosporine-like amino acids (MAAs) were added as a fourth pathway.
The working question was: if a fungal genome carries the genes for a pathway, does the metabolite corpus show the product more often for that species?

3.1 Tool and tables

A Python package, analysis/pathway_census/ (merged to main, merge 1122d5f). It reads a pathway definition (YAML, schema v2: routes, any-of domains, decoys, regions, organism-keyed references) and counts genes per genome.

A compound enters M2 only if all three hold (PROPOSED, accepted by the owner):

section: 7. How to connect this corpus to other data
text:
7. How to connect this corpus to other data

The unit is the accession, not the group. Hold out whole accessions. Collapse the 174 mirrored duplicate groups first (REPORTED).
Stratify by instrument and polarity. Orbitrap positive is the primary stratum. Orbitrap negative and qTOF positive are reported separately only when a cell has at least 6 capable and 30 non-capable accessions (PROPOSED).
Separate yeast from filamentous fungi. Capability, growth form and extraction method are confounded.
Drop genus-only “Fungi” groups (15 of 116).
Define “observed” two ways and report both: library name, and accepted formula plus MS2 class. Formula alone is MSI level 4 at best.
Never match on mass alone. Isobars exist (palythene and usujirene share m/z 285.14; mycosporine-methylamine-threonine and mycosporine glutaminol share 303.154).
Library labels need care. 21.5% of hits are NIST14 spectral-match labels. Two MAA-named groups with a fungal dominant taxon hold non-fungal runs, so the hit cannot be assigned to the fungus.
Run the gate first. Get the detectability counts before building a model. This saved a full comparison here.
Run any SIRIUS comparison with a matched control set processed the same way.
Keep evidence tiers attached to claims. A T3 link is an annotation, not an assay. A route tier that holds only across several organisms is not a tier for any one organism.
Identifiers: KEGG ids are cross-references only (academic licence). ChEBI and PubChem licences for a shared table are UNVERIFIED. Release outside the group is an open owner decision.
Genome gaps: BFD holds fungi only. Bacterial, algal, plant and animal producers need genomes from elsewhere.

text:
8. What would change these conclusions

A compound with at least 6 capable and 3 observing accessions in the primary stratum, and a positive control at 3 accessions, would open M2 for that compound.
Metabolomics of fungi grown for a pigment (induced carotenoid or melanin conditions, targeted extraction) would test H1 and H2 directly. This is outside the corpus.
A matched negative-control SIRIUS run would decide whether class anchors (M3) mean anything.
Fungal genomes with confirmed MAA genes, once Task 6 finishes, would let the marine signal be compared with a fungal capability call.

9. Not done here

No M2 or M3 test was run. No census was run on real data for any curated step set.
No bench work and no chemical identification.
